newsitem.title: USA: TVA seeks antitrust probe of rival U.S. utilities.
newsitem.headline: TVA seeks antitrust probe of rival U.S. utilities.

text.p: The Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) said Wednesday it has asked the Justice Department to look into whether rival, publicly-traded power companies are breaking antitrust laws by seeking to rein in TVA's sales.

"It appears from these private utilities' own documents that their activities are to undermine TVA's ability to compete," TVA General Counsel Edward Christenbury said in a letter to Attorney General Janet Reno.
"(There) may be a question of whether the activities of these utilities are designed to prevent TVA from carrying out its mission under the TVA Act."

TVA, created by a federal mandate in the 1930s, seeks to provide power at the lowest possible cost. It is the biggest supplier of electricity in the United States, with a total generation capacity of 28,123 megawatts and 1996 sales of $5.7 billion.
"TVA's power programme is completely self-supporting, with no federal support of any kind," said spokesman Frank Cason at TVA's Knoxville, Tenn., headquarters.
The letter to Janet Reno comes just six days after Southern Co., Duke Power Co., and a unit of Entergy Corp. filed a lawsuit against TVA in a U.S. District Court in Birmingham, Ala.
The lawsuit alleges TVA has overstepped its federal mandate by using its Tennessee Valley customers as outlets for selling power to customers beyond its designated territory.

The three utilities argue TVA, as a protected agency, enjoys competitive advantages denied to private utilities seeking to expand their own revenue base as the United States moves to deregulate its $200 billion a year electricity industry.

Christenbury, in a statement issued by TVA, said Southern, Duke, Entergy, American Electric Power Co. (AEP), and Carolina Power & Light Co. had formed an association called TVA Watch or the TVA Reform Alliance.

"We are just trying to be sure that when competition begins, it is on a balanced playing field, and that we are not competing against a quasi-government agency that is subsidised and in the marketplace," said Pat Hemlepp, spokesman for AEP in Columbus, Ohio.
"Having one group out there that doesn't exist in the same competitive environment doesn't help, and that is why we are part of the TVA Reform Alliance," he said.
